text: Trade-off analysis: the CAP theorem, for data engineers — and why it's really only ever a choice between two of its three letters.
Consistency, availability, and partition tolerance. The theorem only really says something about what happens during a network partition — outside of one, a well-built system can approach all three.

Any real distributed system will eventually hit a partition — that's a fact, not a choice. So the real question is what a node does when it happens: refuse to answer and stay consistent, or answer anyway and stay available but risk a stale answer.
A single-writer transactional source leans CP — it'd rather error than show an inconsistent balance. A serving-layer cache leans AP — it'd rather serve slightly stale data than return an error.

Real systems rarely sit at a pure extreme — Delta Lake and Cosmos DB offer tunable consistency per operation. The real question is what happens during a partition, for this specific read path. Next up: the first case study, a ride-sharing analytics platform.
